description: Make the run progressive and cheap to iterate on, which is the user's explicit requirement (they cannot supervise closely and want incremental trial and iteration). Three parts. (1) A staged runner that validates the whole machine on near-free hardware before any H200 is touched, plus swappable recipe files so a failed H200 attempt costs one file change rather than a redesign. (2) A checkpoint mirror in S3 so a retry never re-downloads 151 GB from HuggingFace, and a results collector that pulls run output from S3 into results/ in the exact JSON schema scripts/compare-results.sh already parses. (3) Documentation: a runbook with copy-pasteable commands and honest per-stage costs, a postmortem of the failed run, and corrections to the factual errors this investigation found in README.md. Still launches nothing. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: Create scripts/recipes/ holding one env file per candidate SGLang configuration, each a plain `KEY=value` file that launch-bench-ec2.sh sources and folds into the user-data env prelude. Write three, all with `--speculative-algorithm` spelled correctly (NOT `--speculative-algo`, which is what scripts/run-benchmark.sh currently emits and is a likely hard startup failure): (a) h200-tp4-fp4-eagle.env - model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash, tp=4, EAGLE low-latency preset steps=3 / eagle-topk=1 / draft-tokens=4, TP-only with DP-attention explicitly OFF, and the W4A16 Marlin MoE runner path the cookbook prescribes for Hopper FP4; (b) h200-tp4-fp8-eagle.env - model sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 (294.1 GB / 273.9 GiB, the repackaged FP8 weights the cookbook says are H100/H200 only and which unlock DP-attention + DeepEP), same EAGLE preset; (c) h200-tp4-dspark-0731.env - model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` and NO --speculative-num-steps / --speculative-eagle-topk / --speculative-num-draft-tokens, because the cookbook states SGLang reads the DSpark shape from the checkpoint and that this variant is verified on 4xH200. Each file must carry a header comment citing its upstream source and stating the exact checkpoint byte size so the disk guard has a value to check against. Do not invent flags: any flag you cannot find in the cookbook or `sglang serve --help` documentation must be left out and noted in findings.

Create scripts/run-staged.sh, the progressive driver, house style as usual, with --stage taking one of: preflight, plumbing, gpu-smoke, full. Stage preflight = scripts/preflight.sh only, zero cost, no CONFIRM_SPEND needed. Stage plumbing = c5d.large spot (2 vCPU, 1 x 50 GB NVMe instance store, no GPU, a couple of cents per hour) running the real bench-bootstrap.sh with a tiny stand-in payload, which exercises single-disk instance-store mount, S3 log and result streaming, CloudWatch heartbeat, spot-interruption polling, the wall-clock watchdog and self-termination on genuine EC2 metal. Stage gpu-smoke = g6e.xlarge spot (1 x L40S, 1 x 250 GB NVMe, well under a dollar per hour) running the same bootstrap with a small model to exercise docker --gpus all, the NVIDIA runtime, nvidia-smi telemetry, SGLang server startup and a short bench_serving; note README section 9.1 records that SGLang v0.5.12 flashinfer fails on SM 7.5 Turing with KeyError 'sm_75', so use L40S (SM 89) and not a T4 instance. Stage full = p5en.48xlarge spot per the selected recipe. Every stage after preflight must refuse to run without CONFIRM_SPEND=yes and must print its own cost estimate first. Default with no --stage is preflight.

run-staged.sh must also write a stage ledger to results/stage-ledger.json (gitignored) recording for each attempted stage: stage name, run id, instance type, start and end time, instance id, exit status, and the S3 prefix, so a later session can see at a glance which stages have passed and which recipe was last tried. Iteration state must live in the repo and in S3, never only in a chat session - that is the specific failure being engineered out.

Create scripts/mirror-checkpoint.sh: mirrors a HuggingFace repo into s3://<results-bucket>/checkpoints/<repo-id>/ so retries pull the weights in-region instead of re-downloading from HuggingFace. It must resolve the exact byte total via the HF API first (the same query FEAT-001 preflight uses), print the resulting S3 storage cost per month (S3 Standard is about $0.023/GB-month, so ~$3.7/mo for the 159.6 GB FP4 checkpoint and ~$6.8/mo for the 294.1 GB FP8 one) and require confirmation before uploading, support resume via `aws s3 sync`, and verify completeness by comparing the object count and total size against the HF manifest. Document that the mirror is what turns a failed H200 attempt from a 151 GB re-download into a fast in-region sync, and that CHECKPOINT_S3_URI in the recipe files is what activates it. Note in the runbook that the cheapest way to populate the mirror is from the benchmark instance itself during a full run (it already has the weights on NVMe), not from the sandbox.

Create scripts/collect-results.sh: given a RUN_ID, downloads s3://<bucket>/runs/<RUN_ID>/ into a local scratch dir, parses the two bench_serving outputs, and writes results/${INSTANCE_TYPE//./-}_tp${TP_SIZE}_${TIMESTAMP}.json plus the matching _summary.txt using the SAME schema scripts/run-benchmark.sh produces, because scripts/compare-results.sh reads exactly metadata.{instance_type,tp_size,region,timestamp} and, for each of custom_benchmark and official_benchmark, .config.{input_tokens,output_tokens,num_prompts,max_concurrency}, .results.* and .pass. Reuse run-benchmark.sh's threshold logic (TPOT P50 <= 4.5 ms, TTFT P50 <= 1700 ms) and its tolerant key lookups (tpot_p50_ms or inter_token_latency_p50_ms, ttft_p50_ms or time_to_first_token_p50_ms, etc). Verify the shape by feeding collect-results.sh a synthetic fixture under tests/fixtures/ and then running scripts/compare-results.sh against a temp results dir, asserting the table shows real numbers rather than N/A - add that as a case in tests/run-tests.sh. Also confirm and handle what `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --output-file` actually writes: recent SGLang versions append one JSON object per line (JSONL), which `json.load` cannot parse, so the collector must handle the JSONL form and read the last record; state in findings which form you implemented against and why.

Fix the latent bugs in scripts/run-benchmark.sh that this investigation surfaced, keeping the change surgical: rename `--speculative-algo` to `--speculative-algorithm`; stop passing `--dp 8 --enable-dp-attention` unconditionally alongside `--tp 8` (the cookbook states DP-attention is unavailable on the Hopper FP4/Marlin path, so DP settings must be opt-in per recipe rather than defaulted on); change the hardcoded hostPath `/mnt/k8s-disks/0/...` into a variable with the README 9.1 note that HyperPod uses /opt/dlami/nvme/ instead; and make the result parsing tolerate the JSONL output form found in the previous step. Do not restructure the script or convert it away from EKS - it remains the EKS path, and the new scripts are the bare-EC2 path.

Create docs/postmortem-2026-08-07-p5en-run.md recording the failed run so the next session does not repeat it: instance i-0459cbc565ec484f6, p5en.48xlarge, us-east-2a, spot ~$26.67/hr, AMI ami-0b80a5f61a0bca5dd, alive 2026-08-07T15:09:55Z to 2026-08-08T04:24:16Z = 13h14m ~= $353, terminated by the same Kiro role with reason Client.UserInitiatedShutdown. Record the telemetry: NetworkIn 315.32 GB total with two ~151 GB bursts at 08-07 15:15 and 08-08 00:25 (checkpoint downloaded twice), EBSWriteBytes 121 GB for attempt 1 but only 19.21 GB for attempt 2 despite a 150.98 GB download, CPUUtilization peaking at 8.34% of 192 vCPUs and dropping to 0.08% at 15:55, 00:50-00:55, 01:35-01:40 and 02:00-02:20, most hours writing only ~10 MB. Record the primary cause (30.4 TB of local NVMe left unmounted while a single 200 GB gp3 root volume held everything, leaving ~175 GB usable against a 148.6 GiB checkpoint plus a ~12.75 GB image) and the confirmed secondary cause (the instruct checkpoint is FP4-experts and H200 is SM90 with no native FP4). State the caveat honestly: there were no GPU metrics at all, so GPU idleness is a strong inference from CPU, disk and network, not a proof. State that nothing was recoverable: no CloudTrail PutObject, zero self-owned snapshots or AMIs, root volume DeleteOnTermination=true, results/ empty, no commits after 4138e92. Close with a table mapping each failure to the specific mitigation in FEAT-001/FEAT-002/FEAT-003.

Create docs/RUNBOOK.md: the copy-pasteable operator guide. Ordered stage-by-stage commands (preflight -> plumbing -> gpu-smoke -> full), the honest cost of each stage with the arithmetic shown (p5en.48xlarge spot at $26.66/hr in us-east-2a, so the 240-minute MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES ceiling caps a full stage near $107, versus the ~$353 the unbounded prior run cost), the CONFIRM_SPEND=yes gate and where it must be typed, how to watch a live run with no SSH (CloudWatch TpotBench heartbeat, `aws s3 ls`/tail of the streamed bootstrap.log, `aws ssm start-session --target <id> --region us-east-2`), how to read /var/log/tpot-bench/status.json to find the phase a run died in, the recipe-swap loop for iterating after a failure with an explicit ordering recommendation and the reason for it, how to tear down if a run is abandoned, and a short troubleshooting table keyed on the failure modes actually anticipated (disk guard trip, checkpoint fetch stall, server never reaching /health inside the 2400s cold-start window, spot interruption, FP4-on-Hopper kernel error analogous to the KeyError 'sm_75' precedent in README 9.1).

Correct README.md where this investigation proved it wrong, editing in place in the existing Chinese style and keeping every acceptance target untouched. Section 5.4 claims H200 needs a 284 GB FP8 checkpoint: the actual official instruct checkpoint deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash is FP4 experts + FP8 attention/dense at 159.6 GB / 148.6 GiB across 73 files (config.json expert_dtype=fp4, quantization_config.quant_method=fp8), and the ~284 GB figure corresponds to the separate repackaged sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 at 294.1 GB / 273.9 GiB across 55 files; also record that per the cookbook Hopper has exactly two options (original FP4 via W4A16 Marlin, TP-only and no DP-attention; or the FP8 repack, which unlocks DP-attention + DeepEP) and that deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base is pure FP8 but is documented as for further pre-training only and is not a valid chat substitute. Section 9.1 已知踩坑 gains a row for the bare-EC2 instance-store trap that just cost $353, alongside the existing NVMe-path row it should have prevented. Section 12.6 gains the DSpark alternative for the 0731 checkpoint and the note that the correct flag spelling is --speculative-algorithm. Add a short pointer from the README to docs/RUNBOOK.md and docs/postmortem-2026-08-07-p5en-run.md, and to the fact that a bare-EC2 path now exists next to the EKS path in scripts/. Keep the existing 12.12 result matrices as-is: they are placeholders to be filled by real runs and this task produces no measurements.

Run the full verification set and commit everything on branch harden-ec2-bench-runner with a Conventional Commits subject and a Chinese body matching the style of commit 4138e92. Do not push and do not open a pull request.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n` passes for scripts/run-staged.sh, scripts/mirror-checkpoint.sh, scripts/collect-results.sh, scripts/run-benchmark.sh and every file in scripts/recipes/ that is sourced as shell.
`bash tests/run-tests.sh` passes, now including the collect-results fixture case, and exits 0.

The collect-results fixture case proves schema compatibility: after collect-results.sh processes tests/fixtures/, running scripts/compare-results.sh against that output prints actual TPOT and TTFT numbers and a PASS/FAIL verdict, with no N/A in the TPOT P50 column.
`bash scripts/run-staged.sh` with no arguments runs only the preflight stage and spends nothing.

`bash scripts/run-staged.sh --stage plumbing` with CONFIRM_SPEND unset exits non-zero after printing the c5d.large cost estimate; likewise for --stage gpu-smoke and --stage full, each printing its own instance type and estimate.
grep for `--speculative-algo ` (with trailing space, to exclude --speculative-algorithm) across scripts/ returns no matches.
All three recipe files exist, each names its exact checkpoint byte total, and the DSpark recipe contains no --speculative-num-steps, --speculative-eagle-topk or --speculative-num-draft-tokens.
docs/RUNBOOK.md contains the four stages in order, a cost figure for each, and the CONFIRM_SPEND=yes gate.

docs/postmortem-2026-08-07-p5en-run.md contains the instance id, the 13h14m duration, the ~$353 figure, the two ~151 GB NetworkIn bursts, the 19.21 GB versus 150.98 GB disk-full signature, the explicit no-GPU-metrics caveat, and a failure-to-mitigation table.

README.md no longer states that H200 requires a 284 GB FP8 checkpoint without qualification, and now records the 159.6 GB FP4-experts instruct checkpoint, the 294.1 GB sgl-project FP8 repack, both Hopper options, and the bare-EC2 instance-store 踩坑 row. The acceptance targets in section 12.1 (TPOT <= 4.5 ms, TTFT <= 1.7 s, 40000 in, 1500 out, 整机部署) and the section 6.1 benchmark commands are byte-for-byte unchanged.
results/ still contains only .gitkeep in git (no measurement files are fabricated), and `git status` is clean after the commit.
`aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-2 --filters Name=instance-state-name,Values=pending,running` returns empty: this feature launched nothing and billed nothing.
